items.prompt: A decreasing candidate deque has k indexes, then a larger value arrives. Which cost claim is accurate?

options.text: That one update must pop only one index.
options.why: It may remove all dominated trailing indexes.

options.text: The entire algorithm becomes quadratic in all cases.
options.why: Every index can be appended once and removed once, bounding the total.

options.text: One update can cost O(k), while the full scan costs O(n).
options.why: The constant-per-arrival bound is amortized, not worst case for an individual update.

options.text: Each expired index must be scanned again at every later arrival.
options.why: Once removed, that candidate index never returns.

items.explanation: The constant-per-arrival bound is amortized, not worst case for an individual update.
